translations.answer: In the 0.34.0 changelist corresponding to #1384, velocity_limit is used for the explicit actuator/DCMotor model internal torque-speed or no-load speed semantics; velocity_limit_sim is written to root_physx_view/PhysX. PR #1654 establishes these two fields, and PR #1873 clarifies that implicit actuator should not propagate the old velocity_limit to the solver, and should explicitly configure velocity_limit_sim when PhysX is limited. During migration, both values should be printed and the training/trajectory should be regressed, not mechanically treating the manufacturer's no-load speed as a solver hard clamp.
translations.applicability: Applies to actuator limit migration in Isaac Lab 0.34.0; later versions must implement the same target version as the corresponding field name.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and there is formal documentation or precise independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: PR #1509 first writes velocity_limit to PhysX and adds testing.
translations.details.attempts.1: The review pointed out that under load, the motor can enter the other quadrant of torque-speed, and no-load speed should not be directly used as a joint hard clamp.
translations.details.attempts.2: PR #1654 adds *_limit_sim; PR #1873 restores the explicit *_limit_sim requirement for implicit actuator.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Confirm whether DCMotor torque-speed cutoff and physics solver maxJointVelocity need different values.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Upgrade and regression of training curves and joint velocity distribution should be done after #1509/#1654/#1873.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: In this version changelist, velocity_limit is used to express the explicit actuator/DCMotor model internal speed capability, and velocity_limit_sim is used to express the hard speed limit propagated to PhysX; implicit actuator should explicitly use velocity_limit_sim when setting solver limits.
translations.details.environments.0: Original Issue commit b9a49ca, Isaac Sim 4.0.0–4.2.0, Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 4090, CUDA 12.1.
translations.details.environments.1: Semantic separation introduced in Isaac Lab extension 0.34.0 / PR #1654, and PR #1873 further retrogrades the old field propagation for implicit actuator.
translations.details.limits.0: The field semantics continue to evolve; use must be based on the target Isaac Lab version document and source code, not a copy without version.
translations.details.limits.1: tight solver limits may introduce simulation artifacts; values must be derived from trajectory/contact regression, not just based on configuration.
translations.details.limits.2: Do not rely on the training curve image in the PR.
translations.details.outcomes.0: #1384 closed; #1654 and #1873 merged. PR #1654 comment mentions that quadruped users can restore actuator limit to normal values after separation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How should DCMotor no-load speed and PhysX joint hard velocity clamp be expressed?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Real-world speed protection should still be implemented in hardware drivers/safety controller; simulation solver clamp is not a real-world safety limit.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The same velocity_limit field once represented two different physical semantics: actuator no-load speed and solver hard clamp.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Early explicit actuator velocity_limit is not written to root_physx_view; imported joint limit can silently override DCMotor settings.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Using the same velocity_limit both as no-load speed and solver hard clamp leads to community users reporting training disruption or version behavior changes.
translations.source.title: Actuator Speed Capability and PhysX Hard Speed Limit Must Be Separately Configured
translations.terms.2: Solver hard clamp (求解器硬限幅)
translations.terms.3: Simulation velocity limit (仿真速度上限)
translations.title: How Should DCMotor velocity_limit and PhysX velocity_limit_sim Be Distinguished in Isaac Lab?
